verticals.name: Poles and substation steel
verticals.definition: Welded tubular steel poles and structures made in a US plant from formed plate or tube: tapered and multi-sided transmission and distribution poles, substation structures (dead-end, bus and equipment-support steel), and the same plants' lighting, high-mast, traffic, sign and telecom monopoles; bolted lattice towers (angle-member transmission and self-supporting telecom towers) are excluded.
verticals.est_us_plants: approx. 50-90 (inferred; floor of named plants from Valmont, Arcosa, Nucor, Nello, Millerbernd, Falcon)
verticals.weld_intensity: High: every pole has seam welds (often SAW) plus base plates, flanges, arms, vangs and hardware welded by GMAW/FCAW
verticals.part_size_fit: Cell: pole sections up to 60 ft and 48-150 in fit the 2026 cell (60 ft x 15 ft, 55,000 lb); older AW3 limit (72 in dia, 65 ft, 10,500 lb) fits distribution, lighting, traffic and telecom poles but not large transmission bases
verticals.part_variety: High: engineered-to-order structures with part-to-part variation and imperfect fit-up
verticals.hiring_pain: High: Valmont and Arcosa 10-Ks cite welder shortages; open MIG welder postings at Valmont
verticals.demand_outlook: Strong: Valmont NA Utility +23% (Q3 2026), Arcosa converting a wind plant to utility structures, Nucor building three pole plants and a $105M expansion
verticals.path_presence: 4 confirmed: Millerbernd (production), Nello (FAT passed), TransAmerican Power Products (roster; plants in Mexico), Valmont (2021 quote)
verticals.fit_test: pass: mostly welded steel; GMAW/FCAW main process for connections and attachments (long seams often SAW); sections fit a cell; engineered-to-order variety
verticals.reason: Recommend ACCEPT. Strongest Path presence of any vertical (four confirmed pole makers incl. Path's own published pole end-to-end capability), weld-intensive, strong grid demand through 2026 and beyond, documented welder shortages. Caveat: longitudinal seam welding is often SAW, outside Path's GMAW process; Path's fit is base plates, attachments and multi-pass connection welds. Lattice towers excluded (bolted).

verticals.name: Shipbuilding and naval defense
verticals.definition: Welded steel ship and barge structures built in US shipyards and their structural-assembly suppliers: hull blocks, panels, units and modules, foundations and naval components for Navy, commercial, workboat, unmanned-vessel and inland-barge construction.
verticals.part_size_fit: Cell for small steel structures; units and modules need Rove
verticals.demand_outlook: Strong: HII outsourcing +30% in 2026; Saronic $300M Franklin expansion
verticals.fit_test: pass: welded steel (aluminum at some yards, e.g. Saronic); weld process per yard not yet evidenced; small structures fit a cell, big units suit Rove; high variety
verticals.reason: Recommend ACCEPT. Largest Path commitment (HII up to $900M program) plus Saronic and LAD; Rove (2027) targets this vertical. Caveats: aluminum-first yards (Saronic) score low on material; many parts exceed the cell.

verticals.name: Mining and heavy equipment
verticals.definition: Heavy welded steel plate structures for mining, construction and bulk-material equipment made in US plants: buckets, truck bodies, booms, excavator and loader arms, frames, hydraulic tanks and wear attachments.
verticals.weld_intensity: High (inferred: heavy plate attachments; welding is the core step)
verticals.part_size_fit: Cell for buckets, tanks, arms; largest haul-truck bodies may need Rove
verticals.fit_test: pass: heavy welded steel plate; MIG/FCAW typical but not yet evidenced per plant; most parts fit the large cell; high variety
verticals.reason: Recommend ACCEPT. Confirmed customer with a published outcome (85% of work automated), Path names the parts, high-mix heavy plate is Path's sweet spot. Demand outlook and plant count still unknown.

verticals.name: Battery-storage and generator enclosures
verticals.definition: Welded steel enclosures, sub-base fuel tanks, skids and containers for generator sets and battery energy storage made in US plants.
verticals.weld_intensity: High for sub-base tanks and frames; enclosure skins may be thin sheet (inferred)
verticals.part_size_fit: Cell: generator tanks up to 55,000 lb, 60 ft x 15 ft (Path FAT)
verticals.part_variety: High: custom enclosures and fuel tanks
verticals.hiring_pain: High: several welder openings with 20% shift premium (EK Machine)
verticals.demand_outlook: Strong (inferred from data-center and grid load)
verticals.path_presence: EK Machine confirmed (Series E roster + 'Path Lead Welder' posting); Path generator-tank cell FAT
verticals.fit_test: pass for tanks, skids and frames; enclosure sheet-metal skins are a weak fit (thin sheet)
verticals.reason: Recommend ACCEPT. Confirmed customer plus a 55,000-lb generator-tank cell FAT; demand tied to data centers. Overlaps data-center prefab; keep separate because buyers are genset/BESS OEMs and packagers.

verticals.name: Data-center and grid prefab
verticals.definition: Welded steel prefabricated infrastructure for data centers and the grid made in US plants: structural frames and skids, power-distribution and switchgear skids, e-house and portable-substation structures, cooling-unit frames (HAC/CAC containment) and server-rack frames.
verticals.part_size_fit: Cell for frames, skids, racks; large e-house shells may need Rove (inferred)
verticals.path_presence: None confirmed (AMSi and '1872' only in analyst report)
verticals.fit_test: pass for structural frames and skids; enclosure sheet work is a weak fit
verticals.reason: Recommend ACCEPT. Strong demand and Path markets it heavily, but no confirmed customer yet; definition overlaps structural steel and enclosures, so plant-finder must tag by product.

verticals.name: Trailers, chassis and mobile power
verticals.definition: Welded steel heavy-haul and specialty trailers, chassis frames, suspensions and subframes, and mobile power-generation chassis made in US plants.
verticals.part_variety: Mixed: custom heavy-haul high-mix; volume trailers high-volume
verticals.path_presence: TYCROP (Granbury TX is its US plant), Hutchens (2023); Cheetah not confirmed
verticals.fit_test: pass for heavy-haul, specialty and mobile-power chassis; high-volume van/flatbed lines are a weak fit (fixed robots)
verticals.reason: Recommend ACCEPT, scoped to custom and heavy-haul makers. Two confirmed customers but the volume trailer segment is a weak fit.

verticals.name: Bridge and structural steel
verticals.definition: Welded structural steel members and assemblies made in US fabrication shops: building beams, columns, trusses, moment frames, plate girders and bridge components.
verticals.est_us_plants: unknown (coordinator saw ~1,900 AISC-certified companies; not all weld-intensive)
verticals.fit_test: pass for weld-intensive shops (girders, trusses, prefab frames); simple beam cut-drill-fit shops are low weld intensity
verticals.reason: Recommend ACCEPT but run after the customer-backed verticals. Very large plant count makes it a broad, lower-precision list; filter to weld-intensive shops.

verticals.name: Transformer tanks
verticals.definition: Welded steel tanks, covers and radiators for power and distribution transformers made in US plants (tank fabricators and transformer OEMs' fab shops).
verticals.path_presence: None (analyst report names the application only)
verticals.fit_test: likely pass (welded plate tanks); process and part sizes not yet evidenced
verticals.reason: Recommend ACCEPT as a small, high-demand vertical close to poles/substation buyers. Evidence thin; confirm weld process and tank sizes in plant-finder.

verticals.name: Defense ground vehicles
verticals.definition: Welded armor-steel hulls, turrets, frames, armored panels and weapon mounts for military ground vehicles made in US plants.
verticals.path_presence: None confirmed (Lockheed Martin is a customer but product not stated)
verticals.fit_test: likely pass (welded armor steel, GMAW common) but not yet evidenced; few large plants
verticals.reason: Recommend ACCEPT, low priority. Path names tanks and vehicles, but no confirmed ground-vehicle customer and few plants; security limits on public data.

verticals.name: Cranes and lifting equipment
verticals.definition: Welded steel booms, lattice and telescopic sections, frames and carriers for cranes and lifting equipment made in US plants.
verticals.est_us_plants: Manitowoc: nine facilities worldwide (one company only)
verticals.fit_test: pass: welded steel sub-assemblies; part sizes (long booms) may exceed 60 ft
verticals.reason: Recommend ACCEPT, low priority. Path names boom assemblies; few US plants; no customer.

verticals.name: Pressure vessels and tanks
verticals.definition: Welded carbon and stainless steel pressure vessels, storage and process tanks made in US plants (ASME and API work).
verticals.fit_test: partial: welded steel, but code seams are often SAW or TIG; nozzles, saddles and attachments suit GMAW
verticals.reason: Recommend ACCEPT, low priority, focus on GMAW-heavy tank shops. Evidence thin.

verticals.name: Oil-and-gas skids
verticals.definition: Welded steel skids, frames, manifolds and process modules for oil, gas and LNG equipment made in US plants.
verticals.fit_test: pass for structural skids and frames; pipe-spool welding is mostly TIG/root work (weak)
verticals.reason: Recommend ACCEPT, low priority; merge with data-center skids if plant overlap is high.

verticals.name: Truck bodies
verticals.definition: Welded steel dump, service and specialty truck bodies and hoists made in US plants.
verticals.fit_test: partial: many bodies are aluminum or sheet steel (weak fit); heavy steel dump bodies pass
verticals.reason: Recommend ACCEPT, lowest priority, or fold into trailers/chassis. No evidence gathered.

verticals.name: Agricultural equipment
verticals.definition: Welded steel frames, booms, tillage and irrigation structures for agricultural equipment made in US plants.
verticals.demand_outlook: Weak-to-stabilizing (Alamo backlog +6%; Valmont Agriculture sales lower)
verticals.fit_test: partial: welded steel with GMAW, but large OEM lines are high-volume with fixed robots
verticals.reason: Recommend REJECT for now (keep as candidate): weak demand and high-volume production are Path's weak-fit case; revisit for short-line, high-mix makers.

verticals.name: Rail cars
verticals.definition: Welded steel freight railcars and tank cars and their major sub-assemblies made in US plants.
verticals.part_variety: Low-to-mixed: repeat designs in large orders
verticals.demand_outlook: Weak: reduced order volumes and backlog (Trinity 10-K)
verticals.fit_test: partial: welded steel, but high-volume repeat designs (Path's weak fit) and whole cars exceed the cell
verticals.reason: Recommend REJECT: railcar demand is down per Trinity, and the work is high-volume repeat production, the weak-fit case. Revisit sub-assembly suppliers later.

verticals.name: Wind towers
verticals.definition: Welded steel tubular wind-turbine tower sections made in US plants.
verticals.est_us_plants: Arcosa: three wind tower plants (North America)
verticals.part_size_fit: Oversize: tower cans exceed cell width; Rove at best
verticals.fit_test: fail: sections exceed cell limits and seams are submerged arc, not GMAW
verticals.reason: Recommend REJECT: oversize, SAW-dominated, falling backlog. Tubular transmission poles belong in v-poles-substation.

verticals.name: Transmission lattice towers
verticals.definition: Bolted steel angle-member lattice towers for transmission and telecom.
verticals.fit_test: fail: bolted with mechanical fasteners, not welded
verticals.reason: Recommend REJECT: assembled with mechanical fasteners (Falcon Steel). Kept for the record; tubular transmission poles live in v-poles-substation.

why_customers_miss_high.not_found: Most points lost are 'unknown = 0', not a bad fit: weld process not published for 10 of 14 (non-Path sources only); no open welder posting found for 9 of 14; no plant trigger or vertical outlook for 5 of 14; scale unknown for 6 of 14. This back-test was a light pass (1-3 pages per company), shallower than a profiler.
real_rubric_mismatches: Saronic: aluminum-first hulls score 4/20 on material, yet it chose Path (Path's aluminum claim is unconfirmed).
Nello: only submerged-arc seam welding is stated; the process rubric has no option for SAW seams plus GMAW attachments, which is the normal pole-plant pattern.
LAD Services: the company states a welder shortage (GM quote) but the labor rubric only counts postings.
Lockheed Martin and Schenck Process: no plant or part identified, so unscorable rather than a mismatch.
why_customers_miss_high.circularity: Process and trigger points were not taken from Path's own case studies. Material/part-fit for Millerbernd, LAD, TYCROP rests partly on Path's description of the deployment (flagged in reasoning).

back_test_summary.dated_confirmations: Valmont and Schenck (2021), Ameritex (2022), Hutchens (2023) are old references; current use unknown.
back_test_summary.scale_rule: Applied to all: 10 only when multi-plant AND 100+ employees at the scored site are stated; company-wide totals alone give 5.
back_test_summary.demand_rule: Unknown = 0. 8 only where the company's vertical has a stated or inferred demand-outlook row; 15 only for a non-Path plant-level trigger within 24 months.

proposed_weights.decided_by: coordinator (advisor checkpoint required before any change)
proposed_rubric_options: Process: 'SAW seams with GMAW/FCAW on attachments stated' = 75% of the process weight (pole and vessel pattern).
Labor: 'company states a welder shortage (10-K, press, executive quote)' = 60% of the labor weight when no posting is found.
proposed_weights.effect_on_back_test: High rises from 2/14 to 4/14 (EK Machine 84, Valmont 82, Millerbernd 72, HII 70; the last two sit on the 70 line). Still far below two-thirds.
proposed_weights.reasoning: Points move from the components least often public (process, postings) to those that public sources show for nearly every Path customer (steel parts in cell range, custom/high-mix work). The proposed rubric options fix two real mismatches (Nello SAW pattern; LAD stated shortage). But reweighting alone cannot reach two-thirds: most shortfall is evidence depth, so the coordinator should first re-run the back-test on profiler-depth research (job boards, OSHA, site pages) before changing weights, and should not lower the aluminum penalty until Path's aluminum claim is confirmed.
